Her craft

Years of practice, worn lightly

Long before the jewellery and the silk, there were mornings spent on adavus — the same steps repeated until the body no longer had to think about them. Unnimaya started at six years old, and simply never really stopped.

These days she spends her weekdays as a software engineer, debugging in one language and expressing in three others — Bharatanatyam, Mohiniyattam, and Kuchipudi each teaching her something the others don't.

Bharatanatyam

Sharp lines, deep aramandi, and a vocabulary of gesture where every mudra carries meaning. A tradition of fire, held with control.

Mohiniyattam

Kerala's dance of gentle sway and circular motion — soft, unhurried, and deceptively demanding in its restraint.

Kuchipudi

Andhra Pradesh's dance-drama tradition, where quick, lyrical footwork carries the narrative almost like theatre.

Since age 6
That's where the training began — and where the discipline that now shapes every part of her life was first built.
10,544 dancers
Unnimaya was part of the Guinness World Record for the largest Bharatanatyam performance, set in Kochi, Kerala on 29 December 2024, organised by Mridanga Vision Premium Art Magazine.
